# Model specification: gnss 1.0.0

u-blox M8-class GNSS receiver on a UART, as configured and read by PX4 and ArduPilot (UBX protocol). Position, velocity and time come from the common sensor source.

## Features

| Feature | Meaning |
|---|---|
| base | UBX configuration, acknowledgements, version, navigation output. |

## Terms

| Term | Kind | Feature | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| baud_rate | control | base | Current port baud rate; starts at the Devicetree initial-baudrate, changed by UBX-CFG-PRT / CFG-VALSET. |
| protocol_out | control | base | Enabled output protocols (UBX; NMEA output stored, not produced). |
| message_rates | control | base | Per-message output rate (CFG-MSG / CFG-VALSET), e.g. NAV-PVT. |
| measure_rate | control | base | Navigation rate (CFG-RATE), default from Devicetree fix-rate. |
| ack | event | base | UBX-ACK-ACK / ACK-NAK answers to configuration messages. |
| version_info | data | base | UBX-MON-VER answer (protocol version 18.00 as PX4 expects for M8). |
| nav_solution | data | base | UBX-NAV-PVT (and other enabled NAV messages) built from the source. |

## Behaviour rules

| Rule | Feature | Rule text |
|---|---|---|
| ADV-GNSS-B001 | base | Characters are accepted and sent at baud_rate only; after a port configuration with a new rate is acknowledged, the receiver switches to it as the u-blox protocol specification states. |
| ADV-GNSS-B002 | base | Every well-formed UBX configuration message gets ACK-ACK (or ACK-NAK for unsupported ones) with correct checksum; malformed messages are ignored. |
| ADV-GNSS-B003 | base | Each enabled navigation message is sent at measure_rate x its message rate, built from the source sample at that time, with the u-blox field scaling (e.g. lat/lon 1e-7 deg, height mm, velocity mm/s, fix type, satellites, accuracies) and a valid checksum. |
| ADV-GNSS-B004 | base | MON-VER answers with the version strings the drivers check. |

**Timing.** Output is scheduled in model time at measure_rate; transmission takes the UART character times.

**Out of scope.** NMEA output, RTCM input, raw measurements, power-save modes, multi-band signal details
